p: "Now that you have said that an omen is meaningful,
a person should make a habit of eating
at the start of the year gourd and fenugreek, etc."
And from this the Shulchan Aruch says
"When he eats fenugreek he should say,
'May it be Your will that our merits increase,' etc.;
and the custom is to eat a sweet apple in honey
and to say, 'That You renew for us
a good and sweet year,' etc.;
and they eat the head of a sheep, to say,
that the foods signify a good omen
For at the beginning of Creation
the essence of life was words of Torah,
in the manner of what is said (Mishlei 9:5),
and drink of the wine I have mixed,"
which is expounded in the holy Zohar
and the wine of the Oral Torah."
when good and evil became intermixed,
the Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah,
which is "the day of the world's conception,"
to taste only of the good,
just as it will be in the future,
as I heard from our holy Rebbe of Izhbitz,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
who said that in the future there will be
"Of every tree of the garden you may surely eat,
and of the Tree of Knowledge — good —
but evil you shall not eat";
meaning that only of the evil of the Tree of Knowledge
and that then it will become clear
anything but the good within the Tree of Knowledge.
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב.
"And Elokim saw the light, that it was good."
And the name of each thing
So when one eats something called "head,"
and this is its root of life,
it serves as an omen that we will be a head;
and likewise fenugreek, that our merits will increase,
And for the sweet apple in honey,
"That You renew for us a good and sweet year,"
writes an allusion to it from these pesukim:
From the Torah, as it is written (Shemos 15:25),
"And Hashem showed him a tree, etc.,
there He set for them a statute and a judgment";
"A person's sustenance is allotted to him
for it is a statute for Yisrael,
a judgment of the G-d of Yaakov."
"The judgments of Hashem are true, altogether righteous,"
and it is written right after it,
"And they went three days in the wilderness
and in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 60a):
וְכִי מַאן יָהִיב לְהוּ אוֹרַיְיתָא וְכוּלֵּי,
"And who gave them the Torah? etc.;
and we have learned that the Holy One, blessed be He,
שֶׁהָיוּ מוּקָּפִים מִקְּלִיפַּת מִצְרַיִם מִכָּל צַד,
where they were surrounded on every side by the kelipah of Mitzrayim,
לֹא יָכְלוּ כְּלָל לְהַשִּׂיג הָאוֹר ה׳,
they could not attain the light of Hashem at all;
and afterward, at the Splitting of the Sea,
where a maidservant saw at the sea
גַּם כֵּן אַחַר כָּךְ נֶעְלַם מֵהֶם,
that too was afterward hidden from them,
as they said in the holy Zohar (ibid.):
"And afterward they sought to gaze upon
the radiance of the King's glory, etc.,"
וְלֹא יָכְלוּ לִשְׁתּוֹת מַיִם מִמָּרָה (שְׁמוֹת טו, כג),
and could not drink water from Marah" (Shemos 15:23),
for even in words of Torah
they could not feel taste and sweetness,
And as they said in the holy Zohar
which are the words of Torah,
for they could not feel any taste.
"'With mortar' — this is kal vachomer, etc."
for they began to feel taste and sweetness
And as it says in the holy Zohar there,
"There He set for them a statute and a judgment";
it is expounded: "statute" — this is Shabbos;
for Shabbos too is the time
when the words of Torah are engraved in the heart,
and one can feel "the light, that it is good,"
and the sweetness in words of Torah.
"For it is a statute for Yisrael,
a judgment of the G-d of Yaakov";
is the time to feel the light,
as it is expounded in the Tikkunim
"'And there was light' — this is Rosh Hashanah,"
for then the light comes into being,
and then too is the time
to feel sweetness in words of Torah.
And likewise the allusion from the Kesuvim
that the Matteh Moshe cited above wrote,
as it is written, "The judgments of Hashem are true" —
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים
this follows what we have said many times
His statutes and His judgments to Yisrael":
meaning that they feel taste in them.
But regarding the nations of the world it says,
"and judgments, they have not known them,"
for even the judgments they do have,
they cannot bring daas into them.
And regarding them it does not say "and His judgments,"
for the judgment of Hashem Yisbarach
for among the nations judgment is din, strict justice,
whereas with Yisrael it alludes to mercy,
"And Mishpat — this is the Holy One, blessed be He."
And this is "His judgments" that are mercy —
this was given over only to Yisrael,
like the judgment of the Sanhedrin, which is with mercy
And when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbos,
then the time is most fitting
to merit the light "that it is good,"
and to feel taste and sweetness in words of Torah;
and then is the time when they will feel in every food
which is "the light, that it is good."
